feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target brand. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, video, and multi-channel communications.  
- Good credibility signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms make claims believable.  
- Strong positioning: headline, summary, competencies, and project examples consistently reinforce a modern digital platform/communications leader profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create more space for outcomes and make the CV easier to scan.  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results (growth %, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings, adoption metrics) would increase impact.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; footer project formatting is cramped. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several phrases already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a tighter public-sector positioning.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “more than 12 years of experience” with “12+ years’ experience” for brevity and cleaner style.
- Add scale or scope from recent roles to increase impact, e.g., enterprise web modernization for high-volume, multi-publisher public-sector platforms.
- Tighten the second sentence to emphasize leadership across strategy, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery rather than listing too many adjacent functions.
- Possible rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years’ experience modernizing high-volume public-sector websites, governance models, and content operations. Leads enterprise web strategy, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; avoid mixing functions, tools, and sectors in one list.
- Prioritize the strongest, most current differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance/editorial operations, analytics, AI-enabled search, automation/integration, and multimedia.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Use “and” instead of “&” if the rest of the CV favors a more formal style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled…,” and “multimedia production” repeat language from the header.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills almost exactly; consider making one section broader and the other more tool-specific.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a compressed portfolio section and overlaps with recent work experience. Tightening wording and adding clearer outcomes or scope would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Increase specificity where possible: name audience, scale, platform, or business purpose (for example, legislative/policy users, Drupal 10, conference activation).
- Use stronger, outcome-oriented verbs and cleaner phrasing: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong; “continued campaign growth” could become “future campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely repeat achievements already covered in the current freelance role.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; consider replacing it with a less-covered project or adding a distinct result.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with more than 12 years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list rather than a high-impact recent engagement. Tighten it around outcomes, scope, and the most distinctive work not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with client, scope, and level: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4 sharper ones focused on impact: digital systems/workflows/analytics; Drupal campaign builds; governance across channels; AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishers/stakeholders served, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/speed gains, workflow time saved.
- Use stronger verbs and less generic phrasing: replace “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with “led,” “built,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “improved.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with NACo bullets on governance, analytics, and Drupal/web operations; emphasize consulting/embedded leadership and new AI-search work.
- Footer project examples already cover microsites and AI search, so avoid repeating those details verbatim in the main bullet text.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-channel operations.”
- Combine the website bullet into an outcome-led line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific and measurable: add newsletter volume/open-rate growth, follower growth, engagement, campaign results, or production output if available.
- Tighten operations/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not day-to-day.
- Video/programming language also overlaps with older NACo entries; focus here on building the studio and scaling capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong scope and channel breadth, but it reads as a bridge role and overlaps heavily with the later Director of Digital Media entry. Tighten it to emphasize what he directly owned and the systems/content channels he helped establish before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with progression and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing prior to promotion to Director.”
- Combine newsletter/video bullets and make outcomes sharper: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders, and produced a weekly advocacy video update that became a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace “helped” phrasing with stronger verbs: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy and program staff.”
- Clarify workflow impact if possible with metrics: “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve content consistency, turnaround time and coordination across channels.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight, governance, and team leadership already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as expanding/formalizing the series, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating platform/analytics details covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad labels with sharper, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging for mission-driven organizations
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Keep “content leadership” focused on governance, planning, and messaging; leave tools/platforms to Technical + IT and analytics to the analytics skills block.
- If space allows, make one line more senior, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy and communications operations leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Work Experience bullets; avoid repeating channel lists elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent strengths tied to your Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put most relevant/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API/workflow work.
- Remove lower-priority platforms unless they are current job targets; consider dropping SharePoint and Power Pages from this topline line.
- Use “search and discovery experiences” instead of just “search experiences” to sound more outcome-oriented.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT and reads more like a software inventory than a topline capability statement. This section should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, with tools as supporting detail.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Group tools together instead of listing each separately; this improves scanability and reduces redundancy.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, add an outcome-oriented qualifier such as “analytics infrastructure and decision-support reporting” to reflect the NACo impact described in recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating every platform here if they remain fully listed in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing higher-level production capability and recent operational scope rather than generic tool/task labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the studio build and leadership-level work.
- Shorten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid event delivery” unless virtual-only events are a target requirement.
- If space allows, add scale/outcome language elsewhere in the CV, not here, e.g., studio built in-house, recurring advocacy programming, livestream support for major events.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- Tool-level detail here may duplicate “Multimedia & Creative Tools” in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add level/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest, most recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light proficiency/context rather than a bare list: “Drupal (primary CMS) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it reads lighter than the enterprise platforms above.
- Keep ordering impact-based, with Drupal clearly first given the recent 10,000+ page migration and current Drupal consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” under Topline Skills; consider merging or using one section for platforms and the other for implementation skills only.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you add platform-specific evidence.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and slightly more senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: Front-End, Integrations & Deployment
- Rewrite as: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, jQuery (legacy support)
- Put newer/relevant tools before older ones; de-emphasize jQuery by labeling it “legacy support” so the profile feels current.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere or inline: “for Drupal-based public-sector sites,” “deployment automation,” or “serverless edge scripting” to show application, not just tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider trimming one version.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if you want this item to emphasize technical delivery rather than operations tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance to recent work and automation strength: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp”
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If these tools drove meaningful outcomes in recent roles, move impact into experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “Built Airtable- and Power Automate-based workflows to improve cross-team publishing coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if they support a broader systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the role, but this item is too bare and doesn’t reflect the scale of your recent email leadership. It should signal enterprise email/engagement platforms without repeating newsletter achievements already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise email campaign delivery • audience segmentation
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier instead of more tools: lifecycle/journey automation, member communications, or newsletter operations
- Keep platform names first; avoid slash-heavy phrasing if possible: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Don’t restate “newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in the NACo experience entries.
- Be careful with “engagement” language if you can’t support CRM/automation depth elsewhere on the CV.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely repeats the “Topline Skills” analytics section and the NACo work bullets. Make it more capability-led and slightly more specific to senior-level use.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Reporting dashboards • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing)
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with “Reporting dashboards” or “Executive reporting dashboards” to sound more outcome-oriented.
- Consider grouping by function, not just tools: Analytics platforms, reporting/BI, optimization.
- If space allows, prioritize stronger strategic terms over commodity terms: keep KPI design/reporting; drop either SEO or A/B testing if you need to tighten.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly duplicative of “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one version shorter or merge them.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating the exact same framing elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2022 and 2022–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Split into 2 concise bullets focused on execution and team contribution, e.g.:
- Helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia production.
- Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates; provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing by replacing “high-impact” with evidence-based outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version focused on launching/building the capability.
- Avoid repeating website leadership language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and frame it as the foundation for later digital/media leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to lead with the standout outcome: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Compress the rest into one supporting clause: “Coordinated innovation and research projects that supported county-focused programs, policy initiatives and related communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content in support of organizational campaigns and program priorities.”
- If possible, add one metric or scope point: number of episodes, audiences served, program areas supported, or cross-functional teams coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize leadership/operations here; later positions show that progression more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it to named tools plus one concise workflow phrase will read more credibly.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast editing/production
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with “Livestream production” or “Studio production workflows” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Change “Podcast production” to “Podcast editing/production” only if you want to signal hands-on post-production, not just oversight.
